vedic_reference.note: Jagannath is the presiding deity of the Puri Jagannath Temple, one of the most famous and ancient temples in India. He is an avatar of Lord Vishnu and is worshipped as the Lord of the Universe.

data.cultural_impact: Ganesha is a widely worshipped deity and is recognized as the remover of obstacles and the god of new beginnings in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Ganesha symbolizes the power of the individual will and helps in removing obstacles on the spiritual path.

historical_references.reference: Jagannath Temple at Puri is one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites in India. The temple is believed to have been built by King Indradyumna in the 11th or 12th century CE.

Another tradition states that Jagannath was the name of a deity worshipped by the Gangas of Odisha in the 13th century CE. According to this tradition, King Anangabhima III of the Ganga dynasty had installed the present idols of Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra in the temple in 1264 CE.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Jagannath means 'Lord of the Universe'. He is the embodiment of Vishnu, the preserver in the Hindu Trimurti. Worship of Jagannath signifies surrendering to the divine power that governs the universe.
